lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Dratalia. The capital of an empire built on things it took.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Somewhere beneath the Imperial Archive lies a grimoire written in Niran — the magic of the East, carried home in Dratalian ships.

lines.speaker: east_witch
lines.text: You are the translator. The one who can still read the old Niran script.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: ...How did you get into my room?

lines.speaker: east_witch
lines.text: Through a crack in time. Dimension Magic is the only magic Nira has left — and I am the last witch who can use it.

lines.speaker: east_witch
lines.text: Your country stole our knowledge. Mine burned what was left, so no one would remember it. I want it returned. To the people of Nira. In their own language.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Then use your magic. Why come to me?

lines.speaker: east_witch
lines.text: Because Dratalia sealed my power long ago. Today, I can no longer open the rift wide enough to carry a single page.

lines.speaker: east_witch
lines.text: But when I was a child, my magic was untouched. Take this — an hourglass cut from the rift itself.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The East Witch places a cold, violet hourglass in your hands. It hums like a held breath.

lines.speaker: east_witch
lines.text: It reaches back in time — to me, when I was little. Her magic opens the way. Your words bring the meaning home.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: And if I refuse?

lines.speaker: east_witch
lines.text: Then the book stays in a vault, and Nira forgets it ever had a voice.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You turn the hourglass over. Through the glass, the same streets appear — years younger.

lines.speaker: young_witch
lines.text: ...Who are you? Why is there a lady inside my hourglass? You smell like Dratalian ink.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I'm calling from your future. I am here to give something back — your people's book. I need your magic to reach it.

lines.speaker: young_witch
lines.text: My magic? Grown-ups say it's dangerous. They say I should forget it.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Then let's prove them wrong together. You walk through the past, I walk through the present.

lines.speaker: young_witch
lines.text: Fine. But if I set a cube down here, it stays there for years — and by your time it's grown big with magic. Don't trip over it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Arrow keys move you both — her in the past, you in the present. Space summons or takes back a cube. Z to undo, R to restart. Reach the book together.

lines.speaker: young_witch
lines.text: The pages you translated... they talk about my grandmother's spells. I never knew they were written down.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: They were. Then they were shipped to Dratalia and stamped 'Imperial Property'.

lines.speaker: young_witch
lines.text: Imperial soldiers came to the village this morning. They were asking about a witch with a book.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Then stay hidden in your time, and I'll keep moving in mine. Mind the cracks in the present — a cube you leave in the past can seal them shut.

lines.speaker: commander
lines.text: That is far enough, Dratalian.

lines.speaker: young_witch
lines.text: (through the hourglass) ...Who is that? He wears the uniform of Nira. Is he one of ours?

lines.speaker: commander
lines.text: I am the Commander of the Niran Guard. And you are carrying something that does not belong to you.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: It belongs to Nira. That is exactly where I am taking it.

lines.speaker: commander
lines.text: Listen to me. We already gave the magic to the ones who can protect it. Dratalia keeps it safe — far from careless hands.

lines.speaker: commander
lines.text: Please. Do not bring that doom back.

lines.speaker: young_witch
lines.text: Doom? It's our grandmothers' words. How can words be doom?

lines.speaker: commander
lines.text: ...A child's voice, inside that glass. So the old witch really did reach into the past.

lines.speaker: commander
lines.text: Then hear this, little one: words make people think. People who think start to ask questions. Nira is quiet now. Peaceful. Let it stay that way.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Quiet because the people who could read were taken away.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: That star on your chest — it carries the mint mark of the Dratalian treasury. They didn't give you a medal. They paid you.

lines.speaker: commander
lines.text: ...You understand nothing of how a small country survives.

lines.speaker: commander
lines.text: Guards. Take the book. And break that hourglass.

lines.speaker: young_witch
lines.text: Not today! Hold on tight — I'll change the road behind you, here in the past!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In the past, the sky over the strait turns the colour of a bruise.

lines.speaker: young_witch
lines.text: Imperial soldiers behind me. Pirates on the water — they want the book for its price, not its words. And a storm coming in.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: And the Commander's guards behind me, here in the present. It feels like the whole world wants us lost.

lines.speaker: young_witch
lines.text: Then we don't get lost. You read. I open the way. Keep going.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The hourglass runs out. The past falls quiet — and in the present, the grimoire is no longer in the vault.

lines.speaker: east_witch
lines.text: You did it. Every page, in Niran again.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: You did it — the little you. I only found the words.

lines.speaker: east_witch
lines.text: That was always the hard part. Magic can be stolen. Meaning has to be given back.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In a small school in Nira, a child opens a book and, for the first time in a generation, reads it aloud.
